claims.statement: RAD-140 (Testolone) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) and anabolic agent with reported high in vitro binding affinity for the androgen receptor (Ki = 7 nM), selective over the progesterone, estrogen, and glucocorticoid receptors; it is a research chemical, not an approved or licensed pharmaceutical.

claims.statement: A published case report describes idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury in a 26-year-old male following self-administered RAD140 (Testolone) use, presenting with nausea, vomiting, severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and jaundice (ALT 243 IU/L, total bilirubin 4.9 mg/dL); liver function normalized within 2 months after RAD140 was stopped, without recurrence of symptoms.

context.doseText: Exact dose not determinable from the case report; the patient used a liquid dropper formulation the authors note makes accurate dosing difficult (case-report context, not a use recommendation).

extractedEvidence.quote: RAD140 (Testalone) is a novel selective androgen receptor modulator with very limited data currently available on adverse effects related to this compound.

reviewFlags: Single case report - establishes plausibility, not population-level incidence or proven causality.

Independent case reports of RAD-140-associated liver injury exist in other journals (e.g., Ochsner Journal, PMC7535764 covering related SARM products); cross-check those at review for a fuller adverse-event picture.

authority-support: A1 regulator source (FDA warning letter, re-fetched and verified 2026-08-29) added as independent corroboration - it names RAD-140/Testolone products specifically and states liver toxicity has occurred in people taking SARM-containing products, consistent with this case report's finding; it does not itself report this individual patient's lab values, which remain sourced to the case report.

claims.statement: RAD140 was evaluated in a completed Phase 1, first-in-human, multi-part clinical trial (NCT03088527) in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer, supplied as an oral drug-in-capsule formulation, with the stated primary purpose of evaluating clinical safety profile, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics; this is an investigational oncology trial, not evidence of an approved indication or of any performance/physique benefit.

context.population: postmenopausal women with HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer (investigational oncology population)
context.useCase: investigational oncology trial (safety/tolerability/PK), not an approved indication
context.doseText: Part A dose escalation, Part B safety expansion at the maximum tolerated dose (trial protocol description; not a use recommendation).

claims.statement: RAD-140/Testolone is marketed online with claims that it 'carries the benefits of Testosterone injections without all the risks' and 'reduces fat and increases muscle mass,' packaged with suggested bodybuilding cycle lengths and daily dosing; these efficacy and safety claims are not supported by the human evidence located, which consists of a small single-arm oncology Phase 1 safety/PK trial and isolated case reports of serious adverse effects including liver injury - not controlled trials establishing benefit or safety for muscle-building or performance use.
